items.detail: The value it's compared with has a different type, so SQL Server converts customers.email to nvarchar(200) on every row (`CONVERT_IMPLICIT(nvarchar(200),email,0) = @P1`) and, by its own warning, can't seek the index.
items.fix: Make the types match: send the value as non-Unicode text (SqlDbType.VarChar in .NET, sql.VarChar in Node's mssql, a non-Unicode mapping in your ORM), or, if your schema keeps text as Unicode, change customers.email to nvarchar(200). Changing a column rewrites it and the indexes on it.
items.title: A type mismatch on customers.email stops SQL Server from seeking an index
items.verify: Explain again: no CONVERT_IMPLICIT in the plan, and the scan became a seek.
